correctness.rationale: The exact conditional binomial-sum law follows from disjoint unordered edge tests: each edge between colors i and i+1 is queried only for the color-i endpoint, so deficiency indicators of all sources are independent. Multinomial coloring then gives the finite product. Uniform multinomial deviations <=n^(2/3), n p_n^2=o(1), and Le Cam sum-of-squares ->0 give TV-Poisson mean exp(-t) times the sum of predecessor color masses for rarest successors. Since min mass <=1/3, the n p >=3 log n connectivity union bound holds, identifying B_n=0 with primitive-three dynamics from time zero with error o(1). Monotone edge coupling extends zero-one threshold outside fixed t windows. Exact proof distinguishes connected from disconnected graphs; finite tests not relied upon as infinite proof.
